draft.title: Neutral-ramp + accent hex perceptual derivation
draft.principle_summary: OKLCH (Ottosson 2020) decomposes an sRGB hex into perceptually near-uniform Lightness, Chroma, and Hue, already adopted at RATIONALE.md:81 as the palette-generation space. Running that conversion on Solen's four frozen base hexes turns bare LOCKFILE literals into a checkable ramp. The two near-white neutrals, s-border #E4E4E7 (L 0.920, C 0.0040, H 286.3) and s-bg.sunken #F4F4F5 (L 0.967, C 0.0013, H 286.4), share a hue angle within 0.1 degrees of each other: a real two-step Radix neutral ramp (matching the step map already claimed at RATIONALE.md:731), not just an assertion. That hue (286, blue-violet) sits roughly 220 degrees around the wheel from the warm hexes it replaced, E0DDDB (L 0.899, C 0.0043, H 56.4) and F8F5F2 (L 0.972, C 0.0051, H 67.8, yellow-orange region), at matched lightness and matched tiny chroma magnitude. That is the numeric proof behind the qualitative "cool reversal, v2 rule 4" claim stated as an assertion at LOCKFILE.md:40, 44 and RATIONALE.md:126, 129, 327 without ever showing a number: it was a pure hue rotation, not a lightness or saturation change. The accent, s-accent #276EF1, converts to L 0.573, C 0.210, H 261.4, landing inside the canonical blue hue band (roughly 240 to 270 degrees) at a chroma near the sRGB gamut's practical ceiling for that hue. Its OKLCH lightness is the direct mechanical cause of its already-recorded borderline WCAG contrast: a mid-lightness (L about 0.57) blue cannot clear 4.5:1 against a near-white background by much, and clears it even less against an already-light sunken background. Recomputing independently confirms 4.58:1 on white and 4.17:1 on sunken (fails AA), matching RATIONALE.md:110-111's 2026-07-15 measurement within rounding. s-ink #0A0A0A converts to L 0.145, C 0.000: it is a lifted near-black (not L 0), which is why it still reads as pure ink with zero hue bias, since chroma is effectively zero. One caveat carried forward honestly: OKLab hue angle is numerically noisy as chroma approaches zero (a known OKLCH limitation, already flagged at RATIONALE.md:81's own caveat line), so the neutral pair's matching H should be read as directionally supportive of the cool-ramp claim, not as a standalone proof; the warm-versus-cool hexes at matched lightness are the more robust half of the same finding because their hue delta (about 220 degrees) is far larger than any plausible noise floor at that chroma level.
draft.gap: LOCKFILE.md:36, 40, 44, 59 state the four base hexes (s-ink #0A0A0A, s-accent #276EF1, s-border #E4E4E7, s-bg.sunken #F4F4F5) as usage-rule literals with zero derivation: no OKLCH position, no stated relationship between the two neutrals, no stated relationship to the warm hexes they replaced. This is asymmetric with the rest of the token system: s-warning's amber IS derived (LOCKFILE.md:72, explicit HSL twin-of-accent formula, same S/L, hue 40 degrees) and the RETIRED tokens section (LOCKFILE.md:104-114) documents exactly why each superseded token was swapped. RATIONALE.md:731 asserts a Radix 12-step neutral placement (border at step 6, sunken at steps 2-3) but shows no OKLCH numbers proving those two hexes actually sit on one coherent ramp rather than being two independently eyeballed near-white greys that happen to look similar. RATIONALE.md's domain-3 contrast table (lines 103-116) already measures WCAG/APCA pairs correctly and does not need correction, but it treats the accent's borderline contrast as an observed fact rather than tracing it to the color's own OKLCH lightness, so the "why is accent-on-sunken failing AA" question has no mechanical answer anywhere in the docs. Separately, this stream's own key_question cites "accent contrast approximately 3.7:1" as a figure to recompute: recomputing it from the WCAG formula against both white and sunken produces 4.58:1 and 4.17:1, not 3.7:1. No document in _design-system/ contains a 3.7:1 figure for the accent; the nearest neighboring number is the retired green-CTA-on-white ratio of 3.6:1 at SOURCE.md:1025, a different token entirely. The 3.7:1 figure should be treated as an unsourced number and dropped rather than propagated into RATIONALE.

draft.proposed_addition:
DECISION: Solen's four frozen base hexes, converted to OKLCH (Ottosson 2020, the space already adopted at RATIONALE.md:81), form a coherent structure rather than four independent picks: s-ink #0A0A0A sits at L 0.145 / C 0.000 (achromatic, lifted off true black); s-accent #276EF1 sits at L 0.573 / C 0.210 / H 261.4 (canonical blue hue band, near-ceiling chroma for that hue in sRGB); s-border #E4E4E7 sits at L 0.920 / C 0.0040 / H 286.3; s-bg.sunken #F4F4F5 sits at L 0.967 / C 0.0013 / H 286.4. The two neutrals match in hue within 0.1 degrees, confirming they are two lightness steps of one cool-toned ramp (matching the Radix step map already asserted at RATIONALE.md:731) rather than two independently eyeballed greys. Their warm predecessors, E0DDDB (L 0.899 / C 0.0043 / H 56.4) and F8F5F2 (L 0.972 / C 0.0051 / H 67.8), sit at matched lightness and matched tiny chroma but a hue roughly 220 degrees away (yellow-orange versus blue-violet): the 2026 "cool reversal" (v2 rule 4) was a pure hue rotation at constant lightness and chroma, now shown numerically instead of only asserted.

FORCES: showing OKLCH numbers for four already-frozen, owner-approved hexes versus leaving them as bare literals; treating hue-angle agreement at near-zero chroma as meaningful versus flagging its own noise floor.

OPTIMIZES FOR: making the neutral ramp and the cool-versus-warm swap independently checkable (any future neutral addition can be placed on this ramp by OKLCH job the way RATIONALE.md:731 already prescribes for Radix steps, instead of eyeballing a new hex); tracing the accent's known borderline AA contrast (RATIONALE.md:110-111) to its OKLCH lightness as the mechanical cause, instead of leaving it as an unexplained observed number.

SACRIFICES: none of the four hex values change, this section only documents their position; the hue-match finding for the two neutrals is weaker evidence than the warm-versus-cool delta because chroma is near zero for both pairs (OKLCH hue angle is known to be numerically unstable as chroma approaches zero, RATIONALE.md:81's own caveat), so it should be read as supportive, not as standalone proof.

BOUNDARY: this section grounds the four EXISTING frozen hexes; it does not license inventing a fifth neutral, adjusting L/C/H targets, or treating the OKLCH numbers as a formula that would have picked these exact hexes from scratch (they were chosen by owner review across several rounds, e.g. RATIONALE.md:327's v2 rule 4 decision; OKLCH here explains and verifies the pick after the fact, it does not derive it a priori). Also do not carry forward "accent contrast approximately 3.7:1" from any prior brief: recomputed WCAG values are 4.58:1 on white and 4.17:1 on sunken (the sunken pairing fails AA 4.5:1 for normal text, already recorded at RATIONALE.md:111); no 3.7:1 figure exists in any Solen doc for this token and it should not be cited.

MECHANIC: OKLab/OKLCH conversion (Ottosson 2020, T1 for perceptual uniformity, RATIONALE.md:81) applied directly to the sRGB hex via the standard linearize-to-LMS-to-Lab pipeline; WCAG 2.x contrast formula (L1+0.05)/(L2+0.05) on linearized relative luminance (T1, W3C SC 1.4.3, already cited RATIONALE.md:97) applied to recompute the accent pairings. Both are deterministic formula applications, not empirical claims requiring an external study citation beyond the formulas themselves (already sourced elsewhere in RATIONALE.md).

SOURCE: Bjorn Ottosson, "A perceptual color space for image processing" (2020), the OKLab/OKLCH derivation, T1, already the cited authority at RATIONALE.md:81. W3C WCAG 2.1 Success Criterion 1.4.3 contrast formula, T1, already cited at RATIONALE.md:97. Numeric OKLCH and WCAG values in this block were computed directly from the frozen hex literals in LOCKFILE.md:36-59 using those two published formulas (arithmetic conversion, independently reproducible, not a third-party claim needing its own tier).

claim_verdicts.claim: OKLab hue angle becomes numerically unstable as chroma approaches zero
